question: The fallback trained on the 6,409 designs that have measured anchors and serves the other 21,305. How much does that cost?
method: Real trim values for val and test designs from the v2 retraining artifacts, split by whether the design appears in the fallback's training file. Six of the eight targets; lift and distance are not carried in those artifacts.

population.note: Outside designs average far fewer valid speeds - their trim solve converged at only a handful of points, which is why they have no anchors and were excluded from training.

sparse_designs.definition: 3 or fewer valid speeds in 0-50 m/s
sparse_designs.example: design 13077 has one valid speed (12 m/s); the fallback predicts 91 N thrust against a recorded 11.9, and 3,715 W against 387.

conclusion: Retrain on trim data for all 27,714 designs. The row count only grows about 20% - roughly 180,000 valid rows against 149,437 - because the excluded designs contribute few rows each. What changes is that the model finally sees them. Training takes about 20 seconds on a laptop CPU; the missing piece is the data, not the hardware.
